goal:
Redact sealed test code from HTTP evidence surfaces
WHY: Closes F3 note: GET /v1/evidence/{review_id} and provider-call audit records hand the held-out code to any client (the same party that submits the candidate), defeating held-out purpose even after T10.

SPEC: HTTP layer only (direct critic.call_critic() Python return shape unchanged): POST /v1/candidates/review response and GET /v1/evidence/{id} (including nested provider_call records and data/review payloads) strip each sealed test code and return [{kind, code_sha256, code_len}] plus counts; raw code never appears in any HTTP body. Full code stays in the private server store keyed by evidence_id and is the copy T10's runner executes. Chain entries and T11 event summaries already carry ids/metadata only.
Critic constraints: (1) existing tests read main._evidence directly (provider-call audits keep the raw response_document there), so keep raw records in the server store and redact only when serializing HTTP responses (POST /v1/candidates/review, GET /v1/evidence/{id}, anything else that echoes evidence). (2) Tracked tests were already moved to the redacted HTTP shape (test_provider_accounting.py, test_critic_t8_sealed_suite_shape.py). (3) The web Lab displays sealed tests: apps/web/app/lab/page.tsx must show kind + short sha256 + length instead of code, and keep Run enabled from review_evidence_id.

ACCEPTANCE (your own plan): HTTP POST /v1/candidates/review and GET /v1/evidence/{review_id} bodies contain no 'def test_' code but contain per-test kind plus sha256/len and total count; Provider-call audit entries in evidence bodies contain no sealed code; Server run via review_evidence_id still executes the full unstripped suite (passing candidate still PASSes); python -m pytest services/api -q passes (T8 HTTP-shape expectations updated by Critic to redacted form; Python-level critic shape tests unchanged)
OUT OF SCOPE: services/api/evoforge/postgres_kernel.py; services/api/evoforge/kernel_api.py; docs/POSTGRES_KERNEL.md; docs/INTERNAL_KERNEL_API.md; changing the Python-internal sealed-suite shape validator
